newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end at 43-month low ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end at 43-month low ahead of holiday.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks closed lower on Monday and finished the last day of trading this year at the lowest level in nearly 43 months after short-term investors sold and took cash to spend during New Year holidays, brokers said.

The SET index, which moved in the negative territory throughout the session, dropped 4.14 points to end at 831.57 on 4.7 billion baht turnover. The SET fell 35.07 percent since the beginning of 1996 and was closed at its lowest level since June 7, 1993, when the index finished at 827.14.
"The selling pressure remained in the market as investors needed cash to spend on New Year's eve," a broker said.
The SET-50 index dropped 0.78 point to 61.28.
Brokers said short-term investors sold stocks across the board after the market resumed in the afternoon as they needed cash to spend during the New Year holidays.
The market will be closed on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The energy sector fell most, declining 2.57 percent, followed by the finance sector, dipping 1.91 percent.
Securities One topped the active list, gaining one baht to 120. Bangkok Bank dropped two to 191.
